name: Dan McKenzie
role: Medora blacksmith and Billings County commissioner
bio: Dan McKenzie was a Medora blacksmith who formed the firm of McKenzie & O'Brien with Joe O'Brien in June 1884 and that August opened a second shop at Belfield, run by his partner. Early in 1885 he spent three months visiting his home of River John, Nova Scotia. He was on the Billings County ticket in March 1886, was elected, and sat on the new board of county commissioners from May 1886, which first met at his office. In October 1886 he sold his blacksmith shop and Medora property to Alex. Morton and went home to River John.

Dan McKenzie, the blacksmith, has been quite busy of late. He says work is picking up again.
Joe O'Brien will be gone about two months on his eastern trip. Meantime Dan McKenzie is holding down the blacksmith shop.
As soon as Joe O'Brien returns, Dan. McKenzie will take a vacation and visit relatives in the east.
